components.name: FileBackup
components.note: Root. Keep O's structural rule: the restore kit depends on nothing backup-only.

components.name: Operation launch and outcome
components.source: O CMP-002; A CMP-012 (dispatch, cross-location outcome)
components.note: Owns the one outcome vocabulary and the per-location fold.

components.name: Configuration
components.note: Owns both document forms and the cross-location overlap checks at launch.

components.name: Provisioning
components.note: Runtime floor, required component, tool location; never prompts unattended.

components.name: Run record and progress
components.source: O CMP-006; A CMP-014 (progress, run records)

components.name: Backup engine
components.source: O CMP-007; A CMP-002 (backup production, narrower)
components.note: O's engine also holds the guard, removal, check and views; A spread those over top-level components.

components.name: Source capture
components.source: O CMP-008; A CMP-003 (traversal, portability, links)

components.name: Change detection
components.note: A merged capture and change detection; the SRs give them different parents (SR-001/074 against SR-088/105/035/011).

components.name: Exclusive-use guard
components.source: O CMP-012; A CMP-006 (store coordination, top-level in A)
components.note: A puts coordination at the top because its read-generation session (A IF-040) makes readers participants; that design is not recommended (conflict K22), so the guard stays backup-only under the engine.

components.name: Store format
components.source: O CMP-016; A CMP-007 (store representation); A CMP-013 (digest text, volume measurement)
components.note: Shared by every writer and both restore routes; owns the digest text form (see interface cluster I13).

components.name: Restore kit
components.note: One set of requirements binds both routes (both sides agree).

components.name: Entry restoration
components.source: O CMP-019; A CMP-011 (file recovery) + A CMP-008 (content resolution, restore side)
components.note: A's CMP-008 'Content resolution' shared between maintenance and restore is not adopted as its own component: the backup-side index (CMP-013) and the restore-side search (CMP-019) have different forms (O IF-043 against A IF-018) and the kit may not depend on backup-only code. Recorded as conflict K38.

components.name: Container
components.source: O CMP-023; A CMP-016 (container adapter, part_of A CMP-012) + A CMP-015 (licensed image)
components.note: A nests the adapter under launch; O keeps adapter and image together. O preferred: SR-034/130/143 are one delivery responsibility.

interfaces.title: Backup launch request
interfaces.note: Both have it. O is more correct: it names the real switches (-AutoInstallDeps, not A's -AutoInstallHashing), states applicability and the bad-request rule. A lists -DiscardUnreferencedData and -AllowUnverifiedIndex, which are module-level options, not entry switches. Disagree on -WhatIf (removal dry run, K04) and -Deep (K05). Neither lists -IncludeSnapshots or the -VerifyStorage alias that the entry point also accepts; -BackupTime is a test seam and stays out of the form.

interfaces.title: Operation outcome value
interfaces.note: Both: {0,1,2,3,4} with the ruled meanings. O adds the closed list of operations, matching the ruling 'every operation' (A omits the report and the view rebuild).

interfaces.title: Configuration settings catalogue
interfaces.note: Both. A states one row for both forms; O splits catalogue / JSON form / native form (IF-004/005/006, carried_by) and adds the reserved word link and the retired key PreserveFolderTree. Disagree on ConfigVersion (A 3, O 2; K02) and SpaceView type (A off|on, O boolean; K03). BEHAVIOUR FLAG: both state the schedule letters' timing in the form (A elapsed periods, O calendar buckets); the letters' value set is form, their timing belongs to LLR-011 only.

interfaces.title: Native-Windows configuration document
interfaces.note: Both admit a host-protected credential only in this form (owner ruling).

interfaces.title: Environment settings
interfaces.note: O adds FILEBACKUP_LOG_PATH and FILEBACKUP_NO_GUI (both read by today's code). A's discovery-source order is behaviour and belongs to LLR-037.

interfaces.title: Run record
interfaces.note: Both. O concrete (names, entry grammar, prefixes). FLAG: O's refusal tokens embed requirement ids ([SR-075/...]); they exist in today's code, so keep them frozen as form but do not mint new id-bearing tokens (requirement renumbering would change a host-visible string).

interfaces.title: Machine-readable findings
interfaces.note: Both. O matches the code's field names (Class, FolderName, KitRevision; A says Kind and invents WitnessMismatch/UnsupportedForm where the code has LegacyStoredForm). O adds Repaired for SR-104 (gap). A adds that BytesReclaimed may be negative; keep that as a stated value range if the plan can yield it.

interfaces.title: Backup store layout
interfaces.note: Both. A states roles without names and puts the leaf names into LLRs (K36); O names them in the form, which the brief allows and which gives each name one home. A's IF-041 (B-02 live storage exchange) folds in as O's second crossing. BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: 'the date is the completion time of the state it holds' and 'the retired launcher name is never written' move to LLR-028 and LLR-007.

interfaces.title: Record of contents
interfaces.note: Same nine columns, both backslash separators (today's Linux writer uses '/', gap M42). A adds canonical bytes (LF, BOM tolerated on input, Length range, Duplicate may be empty); O adds Original as the retired layout-marker value and the boundary crossing. Union.

interfaces.title: Completeness evidence
interfaces.note: Same keys today (Version=2, Rows, Bytes, XxH128, Written; A matches the code). O proposes Version=3 with DirRows/LinkRows as positive age evidence.

interfaces.title: Stored object name and form
interfaces.note: Same grammar and alphabet. O is correct that a compressed object's extension becomes .7z (A's 'outer .7z suffix' reads as appended); O adds the retired grammars the code recognises (separator in name; space at index 16 in 27+ characters). BEHAVIOUR FLAG: 'the electing file's extension' is LLR-058's decision.

interfaces.title: Folder record
interfaces.note: A's semicolon separator contradicts today's comma (both routes split on ','); changing it breaks kits already in backups (SR-084). A's always-present header-only record against O's present-only-with-rows (today's behaviour).

interfaces.title: Link record
interfaces.note: Both new form, separate file LINKS.csv. Column names and value sets differ.

interfaces.title: Restore kit artifact set
interfaces.note: O names the on-disk artifacts that are data or launchers and names the kit's code files by role (correct per brief). BEHAVIOUR FLAG: the launcher's 'one line passing every argument' is LLR-074's.

interfaces.title: Restore request
interfaces.note: O gives the real switches of both routes; A abstract.

interfaces.title: Restore outcome value
interfaces.note: Same value set.

interfaces.title: Restore report
interfaces.note: O's cause tokens match the code. BEHAVIOUR FLAG: 'nothing is written to the target before admission passes' is LLR (admission) text.

interfaces.title: Restore tool floor
interfaces.note: A's 'POSIX byte-count fallback' is behaviour (LLR-071).

interfaces.title: Restore target probe
interfaces.note: A adds allocation-unit bytes and target name/attribute/link semantics, needed by the declared allowance (K09) and collision detection.

interfaces.title: Source tree view
interfaces.note: Same. BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: 'read-only opens that share reading only' belongs to the source-never-changed LLR.

interfaces.title: Change-detection record
interfaces.note: A splits the external location (B-20) and the source-root cache (B-24) and adds a source/store identity binding and generation id (new form); O one row on both crossings, no new fields.

interfaces.title: Run-state record
interfaces.note: A adds a state-generation identity and source/store binding (new form, tied to K12/K20). BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: 'written to .tmp and published by rename' is LLR-028/087 text; the .tmp name itself is form.

interfaces.title: Volume space and identity
interfaces.note: A adds allocation-unit bytes. BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: the mount-table rule is FileBackup's measurement (LLR for volume identity), not the external party's form.

interfaces.title: Exclusive-use claim
interfaces.note: Same artifact (Temp.lock at the saved-state root). BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: 'never written and never deleted' is LLR-093's.

interfaces.title: Staging area and owner record
interfaces.note: Same fields as the code. A puts the classification verdict in this row; O moves it to the internal IF-044 (better: verdict is a result, not the record). Add: PRUNE.inprogress holds the saved-state name as text. BEHAVIOUR FLAG in O: 'written once by exclusive create', 'modification time is the liveness evidence' belong to LLR-080.

interfaces.title: Content digest
interfaces.note: Both: XXH128, 32 uppercase hex, most significant byte first. Owner differs: A CMP-007 (internal store representation), O external:EXT-06. Recommend owner CMP-016 for the text form, which is FileBackup's choice, with the hashing service itself in IF-046. FLAG: O names the third-party package; move the package identity to IF-037.

interfaces.title: Package source
interfaces.note: O pins 8.0.0 identified by the published SHA-256 (as the image build does today); A allows 'a declared compatible release'.

interfaces.title: Container actions and environment
interfaces.verdict: take O + A values, conflicts K04, K25
interfaces.note: A's truthy set (1,true,TRUE,True,yes,YES,Yes) matches the entry script exactly; O's 'any case' is wrong. A keeps FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN; O drops it.

interfaces.title: Container mounts and user
interfaces.note: O names the mounts and uid 65532 and adds /tmp scratch (the shipped compose file mounts /tmp as tmpfs).

interfaces.title: Space view
interfaces.note: New form both sides; O concrete (SPACE.tsv).

interfaces.title: Content-location index (internal)
interfaces.note: O only. A's nearest is IF-018 (per-key query), a different form.

interfaces.title: Leftover classification verdict (internal)
interfaces.note: A carries the verdict set inside its owner-record row.

interfaces.title: Content search by key (internal, restore side)
interfaces.note: A only. O states the same answer set in LLR-050 text; a typed, symbol-free form is the target shape for a call that crosses components. Owner CMP-019.

interfaces.title: Backup runtime and tool floor
interfaces.note: A states the backup-side runtime floor at B-10; O states it only in LLR-020. Owner external:EXT-06.

interfaces.title: State format descriptor and publication intent
interfaces.note: A only (STATE-FORMAT.json plus a durable intent). Adopted only if K14 or K20 goes A's way.

interfaces.title: Read-generation session
interfaces.note: A only. Adopted only if K22 goes A's way.

llrs.cluster: Every operation ends with one value of the shared vocabulary
llrs.note: O adds the full operation list (report and view rebuild included, per the ruling 'every operation'), the precondition list and the unclassified-error rule (2 before any change, 4 after). A adds nothing O lacks. Move the multi-location fold out (to LLR-014) so it has one home.

llrs.cluster: Configured locations run independently and fold into one value
llrs.note: O carries the fold rule; A adds that the full location set is resolved and validated before admission and that a multi-location configuration draws no warning.

llrs.cluster: An unattended operation never asks
llrs.note: Same obligation; O enumerates the session signals and the per-operation scope. Today redirected or closed input is not detected (gap M15).

llrs.cluster: The report and the check write one findings document on standard output
llrs.note: A states SR-104 only through interface forms and the sr_refs of its check and report rows. O adds 'nothing else on standard output' and the repaired flag.

llrs.cluster: Container actions map onto the same request and outcome
llrs.note: A also bundles mounts and identity (moved to the container-access cluster) and keeps the dry-run variable; O forces notification off and the unattended declaration (both true of today's entry script).

llrs.cluster: Configuration validated against the one catalogue before anything is touched
llrs.note: A's row carries five SRs (018, 042, 123, 135, 129); split per O so each SR's obligation has its own row. Both: closed keys, kind-checked values, first fault in document order, defaults materialised.

llrs.cluster: A configuration location naming no document is refused
llrs.note: A merged this into LLR-042; the legacy meaning survives and O's child adds 'creates nothing, the global record included'.

llrs.cluster: A retired setting is refused by name, as retired
llrs.note: A retired LLR-063 into LLR-042 text; SR-018's AC names the retired-by-name message, a distinct decision.

llrs.cluster: An older supported description version keeps its meaning
llrs.note: A states a version-specific meaning table inside LLR-042.

llrs.cluster: Every configuration document states its description version
llrs.note: A inside LLR-042. O adds that the helper writes the current version.

llrs.cluster: A configuration carrying a readable credential is refused
llrs.note: A inside LLR-042 and LLR-104.

llrs.cluster: The published description and the launch checks give the same verdict
llrs.note: A inside LLR-042 and LLR-027.

llrs.cluster: The shipped example configuration is accepted
llrs.note: A inside LLR-027.

llrs.cluster: Configured locations may not overlap a source or the store
llrs.note: Both physical, across every set, before anything is created. O adds drive-root sources, foreign content left in place, and 'listing location not on the backup's volume' (today's code; no SR asks, K35).

llrs.cluster: A read-only source with no state location elsewhere is refused up front
llrs.note: A inside LLR-095 (names the SourceStatePath setting). O: an access query that writes nothing, no probe file.

llrs.cluster: Tool locations and compression effort
llrs.note: Same precedence and the exact single-digit rule; O adds that reading the effort never raises (the restore-safe library reads it), A that restores and non-compressing actions ignore an invalid value (both say so).

llrs.cluster: The runtime and every needed tool are checked before any location is touched
llrs.note: A also covers SR-132 (moved to the next cluster). O adds the runtime floor; neither side's code has a runtime check (gap M14).

llrs.cluster: The hashing component is obtained on first use, or the launch is refused
llrs.note: A inside LLR-020 ('the permitted package fetch').

llrs.cluster: A run's outcome is sent where set up; a send failure changes nothing
llrs.note: Same; O adds login only where the configuration carries one (owner ruling: SMTP login only where the server needs one).

llrs.cluster: Notification credentials are never written in readable form
llrs.note: A adds sanitising provider failures; A's SR-129 part goes to the readable-credential cluster.

llrs.cluster: No record is created or truncated before the configuration is admitted
llrs.note: A states 'before creating or changing any location or log' inside LLR-042 and lists appending as a gap.

llrs.cluster: Each run's record names every change and failure, with counts
llrs.note: A's LLR-103 carries four SRs (124, 125, 126, 089); split per O.

llrs.cluster: Progress at least every two minutes of active time
llrs.note: Same in A LLR-103.

llrs.cluster: Every refusal states what was found and what to do
llrs.note: Same in A LLR-103; A's secret-sanitising clause goes to the credentials cluster.

llrs.cluster: Every entry is walked; only the declared exclusions are left out
llrs.note: A's LLR-001 also states change detection (moved to the change-set cluster) and SR-089 naming (moved to the uncapturable cluster).

llrs.cluster: Volume system folders are left out only at a volume-root source
llrs.verdict: take O (child of LLR-001) + A clause
llrs.note: A adds that an unknown volume-root status defaults to capture; O that every store enumeration applies the same test.

llrs.cluster: A name invalid on Windows or Linux is refused and named
llrs.note: O adds that a non-portable folder name is left out of the folder record with a warning.

llrs.cluster: Folder links: followed outside, recorded inside or into own locations
llrs.note: One classification decision (O); A splits following (105) from recording (106). A adds the 60-second bounded wait per remote request (K18); O adds the ancestor test 'inside a followed outside folder too'.

llrs.cluster: A recorded link carries its kind and where it led
llrs.note: A states it inside LLR-106.

llrs.cluster: A briefly unreadable file is retried within a bounded per-location limit
llrs.note: Same values (3 attempts, 250 ms then 1000 ms, 60 s per location, a folder at the destination is permanent); both cover the digest read, which today's code does not (gap M29).

llrs.cluster: A file or folder that cannot be captured is named and keeps its earlier content
llrs.note: A states it across LLR-001, LLR-055 and LLR-067.

llrs.cluster: Empty and attributed folders are recorded
llrs.note: A's LLR-065 also applies the record at restore (split to the folder-application cluster).

llrs.cluster: A run never changes the source
llrs.note: A's row also carries SR-094/139/148 (to the record-location cluster).

llrs.cluster: A source that suddenly looks empty is refused unless declared
llrs.note: Both value 2. O adds that a source whose only files were left out still counts as showing files; A that an unreadable source is distinguished from an empty one.

llrs.cluster: Source-derived paths are taken literally
llrs.note: A's cross-host clause moves to the one-store-form cluster; A constrains IF-014, O nothing (an LLR need not name an interface).

llrs.cluster: The change set comes from size, time and, when re-read, content
llrs.note: A states it inside LLR-001 and LLR-011 (O split legacy LLR-001's diff out because it serves different SRs).

llrs.cluster: The re-read schedule decides the same way every time
llrs.note: SR-011 says 'at or after its period has elapsed since the last completed full re-read': A's elapsed periods meet it, O's calendar buckets follow today's code. A also keeps N as never with no history (the code re-reads).

llrs.cluster: An unusable change-detection record is rebuilt from the backup's own record
llrs.note: A binds the record to a source/store identity and generation (new form); O reconciles per path against the backup's latest record. Both log the rebuild.

llrs.cluster: The change-detection record lives at the source root unless configured elsewhere
llrs.note: A inside LLR-096.

llrs.cluster: A missing run-state record never makes a populated backup a first backup
llrs.note: A states it inside LLR-028 ('recover the prior state date from durable evidence or refuse').

llrs.cluster: A saved state is named by the completion time of the state it holds
llrs.note: Both: written after publication, before the collapse; today the name comes from the previous run's start time (gap M06, found by O only).

llrs.cluster: Identical content is stored once
llrs.note: A adds that a blank or missing location is demand, not supply (shared with LLR-053).

llrs.cluster: Each content group has one owner and one stored form, decided once
llrs.note: Same election (shortest path, ordinal tie). A adds create-through-temporary-then-publish without replacing a claimed object (see K33).

llrs.cluster: A stored object is never merged into leftovers at its name
llrs.note: A's private-temporary publication in LLR-058 serves the same hazard.

llrs.cluster: Lost content is stored again; adoption needs content actually present
llrs.note: Same.

llrs.cluster: Compression decided by measured saving, by file type where nothing is measured
llrs.note: Same order and values (floor 256 KiB inclusive, 0.90 aggregate); O adds the decision's reason names. Today a file of exactly 262144 bytes is probed (gap M57, found by A only).

llrs.cluster: One list of already-compressed types is the file-type rule
llrs.note: O's child structure, A's explicit list (the values need one spine home).

llrs.cluster: The measurement samples three windows and never fails a run
llrs.note: Same geometry and bounds; A names the codec (fastest Brotli level), O describes it. Keep the named algorithm: it fixes the measured ratio, and it is not a code symbol.

llrs.cluster: A backup refuses before writing when a volume lacks the space it needs
llrs.note: Same demand terms and value 2. Disagree on an unmeasurable volume, on declared allowance values and on when the plan runs.

llrs.cluster: Volume identity and free space are measured the same way on every host
llrs.note: A states it in IF-019/020 data and its capacity rows.

llrs.cluster: A changing run keeps the previous state; an unchanged run adds none
llrs.note: A adds folder-only and link-only changes to the change set (today a new empty folder alone adds no saved state, gap M48).

llrs.cluster: Content leaves the latest state only when no final-record entry claims it
llrs.note: Same rule at both removal sites; A merged legacy LLR-006 and LLR-059 into it.

llrs.cluster: Superseded content is kept with the saved state
llrs.note: A merged it into LLR-051; O's row states the preservation itself, which the claim test does not.

llrs.cluster: Earlier content stays reachable until the replacing state is published
llrs.note: A states it inside LLR-115 and LLR-041; O misses it. Today removed and superseded objects move into the staging area before the new latest record is published, so a kill there leaves a witnessed record whose bytes only staging holds (gap M53, confirmed in code).

llrs.cluster: Earlier content that cannot be placed stays restorable, and the run fails
llrs.note: Both: continue per file, report part failed, publish no saved state missing content.

llrs.cluster: A record is published whole or not at all
llrs.verdict: take A on durability; conflict K19
llrs.note: A flushes before the rename; O says it does not, accepting a torn newest record after power loss, which SR-082's AC forbids.

llrs.cluster: An interrupted publication is completed when positively identified
llrs.note: O: evidence temporary written before the record rename; A: a durable publication intent with old/new identities.

llrs.cluster: Every record carries its own completeness evidence
llrs.note: O adds the folder- and link-record row counts to the evidence.

llrs.cluster: Every state carries a restore kit
llrs.note: A adds 'before the state is visible' and the kit's closed dependency set; A's SR-131 part goes to the notices cluster.

llrs.cluster: Third-party components travel with their licences and notices
llrs.note: A inside LLR-007.

llrs.cluster: No write leaves an existing kit unable to read its state
llrs.note: A spreads SR-084 over LLR-060, LLR-076 and LLR-111.

llrs.cluster: One kit revision, moved whenever a kit file changes behaviour
llrs.note: A's coherent-refresh clauses move to the kit-refresh cluster.

llrs.cluster: Content duplicated across saved states is collapsed to one copy
llrs.note: A adds: remove a redundant copy only after the keeper is verified and every dependent state still resolves (a SR-059 safeguard O lacks).

llrs.cluster: Every host writes and continues one store form
llrs.note: Both choose the backslash separator (A in its record form); only O lists the gap (today's Linux writer uses '/') and the migration it causes.

llrs.cluster: One changing operation at a time holds the backup through the OS claim
llrs.note: Same primitive (3 attempts 250 ms apart, never unlinked). A also states the failure classes (split to the next cluster).

llrs.cluster: A claim that cannot be taken is classified and touches nothing
llrs.note: Same values in A LLR-090 (contention or I/O 4; denial or unusable location 2).

llrs.cluster: A backup holds the claim from its first store read to its last write
llrs.note: A's LLR-091 also absorbs removal, repair, refresh and the reader rule; split per legacy ids.

llrs.cluster: A removal holds the claim for its whole batch
llrs.note: A merged it into LLR-091; each window has its own start and end point.

llrs.cluster: A repair and a kit refresh hold the claim
llrs.note: A merged it into LLR-091.

llrs.cluster: The claim file is never deleted and is invisible to every reader
llrs.note: A states it in LLR-090 and LLR-022.

llrs.cluster: Checks, the report and restores take no claim and still complete
llrs.note: A adds a pinned read generation and writer-side deferral (new IF-040); O relies on published states not changing in place, which repair, collapse and removal contradict.

llrs.cluster: An earlier run's leftovers are classified from the disk alone
llrs.note: Same classes and precedence (2 over 3 over 4). A adds the unchanged second sample here; O in LLR-080.

llrs.cluster: Record publication temporaries are not content
llrs.note: Legacy LLR-088 means the staging allowlist; O kept that meaning. A reused the id LLR-088 for the move-aside reclaim (next-but-one cluster) and minted LLR-110 (child of LLR-022) for this; keep LLR-088 with O's meaning and A's root-scoped, case-exact detail.

llrs.cluster: A backup's owner record and its age are the liveness evidence
llrs.note: Same 60 s refresh and 1800 s floor. A is a child of LLR-017; O is top-level because it serves SR-075, not SR-017 (O's rule, adopted).

llrs.cluster: A provably dead run's leftovers are reclaimed by moving them aside
llrs.note: Same protocol (move aside, re-check identity, fresh staging and record, non-recursive delete, keep on any surprise).

llrs.cluster: A run whose claim was lost changes nothing more
llrs.note: A fences before every mutation; O at five fixed boundaries.

llrs.cluster: Content only the removed state holds is re-homed first
llrs.note: Same election and verification; both refuse a conflicting destination and reuse an identical one.

llrs.cluster: A removal that could lose content is refused before anything changes
llrs.note: Both collect every cause; values per SR-046 (3 only for failing evidence alone, else 2). A's confinement clauses move to the next cluster.

llrs.cluster: A removal is confined to the chosen backup
llrs.note: A inside LLR-046.

llrs.cluster: An interrupted removal loses nothing and completes when re-run
llrs.note: A adds resuming the removal's own pre-commit work (today a killed pre-commit removal wedges on its own staging marker, gap M51, found by A only).

llrs.cluster: The saved-state report gives what each removal would free and move
llrs.note: Same: figures from the removal's own plan.

llrs.cluster: The report and a check without repair change nothing
llrs.note: A inside LLR-047 and LLR-049.

llrs.cluster: Whole-backup passes grow with the entries; the index with the stored objects
llrs.note: Same linear reference-set audit with filesystem case semantics; O adds the lean index default.

llrs.cluster: A run's work follows what changed, within the memory bound
llrs.note: A adds numbers (index bound 1 GiB, one archive job at a time) and a spill mechanism; keep the numbers, drop the spill until a measurement shows the need (orphan iii part).

llrs.cluster: A check reports every disagreement between records and what is stored
llrs.note: Both make reading every distinct stored object once the default check.

llrs.cluster: Missing content is told apart from content missing only from its place
llrs.note: A states it in LLR-049's dimensions only.

llrs.cluster: A repair corrects only what is certain
llrs.note: Same three certain classes and copy-back with a hash before use (owner ruling).

llrs.cluster: An interrupted repair or kit refresh leaves every state restorable
llrs.note: A covers it in LLR-115 and LLR-076.

llrs.cluster: A kit refresh places the current kit in every state and changes nothing else
llrs.note: A inside LLR-076.

llrs.cluster: A store or state in a retired or unrecognised form is refused by name
llrs.note: Both value 2 with a fresh-location remedy, a check reports only, a damaged entry is not a retired store, the retired test is positive.

llrs.cluster: Stored names are encoded, decoded and parsed one way
llrs.note: Same.

llrs.cluster: Where turned on, the browse view lists every path
llrs.note: O adds that a rebuild wipes only a folder already holding a generated view (SR-063).

llrs.cluster: Where turned on, the space view lists files by stored size
llrs.note: A's LLR-097 carries four SRs; split per O.

llrs.cluster: The space view gives a media encoding rate where a playing time is measured
llrs.note: A inside LLR-097.

llrs.cluster: A media measure not taken changes nothing else, and says so
llrs.note: A inside LLR-097.

llrs.cluster: The content digest is computed and written one way everywhere
llrs.note: Same.

llrs.cluster: Infrastructure names count only at a folder's own root
llrs.note: A adds the source-root rule (backup-only names there are owner content), which SR-074's AC states.

llrs.cluster: Records are read and written one way, on every route
llrs.note: A: an absent record is not an empty state and refuses; O: it reads empty only where the run-state record shows no earlier backup. Compatible; keep both.

llrs.cluster: An unchanged re-run writes an identical record
llrs.note: Same.

llrs.cluster: A stored item's form is decided from its bytes
llrs.note: A makes it a child of a multi-SR LLR-008 (K29).

llrs.cluster: Every whole-restore check is made before anything is written
llrs.note: Same order; A adds deciding the archive-tool need from actual content forms.

llrs.cluster: A restore target inside the backup is refused
llrs.note: Both value 2, physical, separator boundary. A's SR-141 part goes to its own cluster.

llrs.cluster: Containment compares physical locations and refuses rather than guesses
llrs.note: A merged LLR-079 and LLR-072 into LLR-009.

conflicts.astra: Elapsed periods since the last completed full re-read; N never re-reads, history or not; the time is stamped only when a full re-read completes.
conflicts.opus: Calendar buckets in host-local time (day, ISO week, month, year differ), as today's code; a run with no completed re-read re-reads.
conflicts.bearing: SR-011 (AC: 'at or after its period has elapsed since the last completed full re-read'; 'a never schedule never does').
conflicts.recommendation: Take A. SR-011 decides it; O followed the code. Today N with no history re-reads and the time is stamped whenever a re-read was due, even partly (gap M07).

conflicts.astra: Bump to ConfigVersion 3 (adds SpaceView, uniform versioning); keep a v2 meaning table; asks whether calendar scheduling is v2's meaning.
conflicts.opus: Stay at 2: an optional key with a meaning-preserving default does not bump (the published description already says so of CompressProbe).
conflicts.bearing: SR-123, SR-135, SR-011, SR-097; ruling 'Configuration: version stated, unknown keys refused'.
conflicts.recommendation: Stay at 2. The documented v2 meaning of D/W/M/Y is 'daily, weekly, monthly, yearly', which elapsed periods satisfy, so SR-011's rule does not change v2's meaning; SpaceView defaults off. If the Owner reads calendar buckets as v2's meaning, SR-123 forces version 3 with two schedule semantics kept forever.
conflicts.level: OWNER (what a v2 document means; integrators see the version)

conflicts.astra: Enum off|on.
conflicts.opus: Boolean, default false.
conflicts.recommendation: Boolean, matching AllowEmptySource and CompressEnabled; BrowseView is an enum only because it has a second non-off value.

conflicts.astra: Kept: -WhatIf with Prune and FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN in the container.
conflicts.opus: Dropped: code beyond the design; -WhatIf becomes a bad request.
conflicts.bearing: No SR asks for it; listed as a possible missing need at the SR merge. Implementation-born.
conflicts.recommendation: Do not drop silently: it is a working, documented feature a host may call. Either the Owner adds a need (then a dry-run LLR and the form stay) or it is retired with a release note. Until ruled, keep it out of the LLRs and list it under code beyond the design.
conflicts.level: OWNER (removes a feature hosts can see)

conflicts.opus: Full payload check is the default; -Deep dropped from the form.
conflicts.bearing: SR-049 (altered content must be reported), SR-064 (8 h budget; about 3 h of reading at the reference host).
conflicts.recommendation: Both agree on the default, so SR-049 settles it. Keep -Deep accepted with no meaning, like -ExitCode, so existing callers are not refused.
conflicts.level: design (coordinator); the cost change is worth telling the Owner

conflicts.astra: -DiscardUnreferencedData and -AllowUnverifiedIndex listed as launch switches.

conflicts.bearing: SR-046 refuses those cases without exception. The entry point has no such switches today.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. A's switches do not exist at the entry point; retire the module overrides or keep them test-only.

conflicts.opus: Fetched without a question, attended or not; -AutoInstallDeps accepted with no meaning.
conflicts.bearing: SR-132 ('attended or not, either obtains it ... or is refused'); SR-016.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. Today attended runs prompt and unattended runs need the switch (gap M15).

conflicts.topic: A volume whose free space cannot be measured (backup and restore)
conflicts.astra: Refused with 2 (needed, free and volume named).
conflicts.opus: Not refused; the record says the check was not made (today's behaviour on both routes).
conflicts.bearing: SR-052 and SR-023 refuse only when demand exceeds free space; silent on unknown. Ruling: 2 = precondition not met.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. Refusing on unknown would stop every run on a share or mount that hides its free space, a precondition the owner cannot always fix; the record line keeps it visible.
conflicts.level: OWNER (changes the outcome an owner sees on such hosts)

conflicts.astra: Declared numbers: allocation rounding (observed unit, else 64 KiB), 4096 bytes per folder and per record entry, 16 MiB fixed, twice the largest expanded object (restore) or the largest temporary objects (backup).
conflicts.opus: 'A declared allowance' without numbers; restore scratch is the largest compressed item's expanded size.
conflicts.bearing: SR-052, SR-023 ('a declared allowance').
conflicts.recommendation: Take A's numbers: an allowance the SR calls declared must be stated somewhere; review the values in round 4 against the harvested test edges.

conflicts.topic: When the backup's space plan runs

conflicts.opus: After the change set is known and before anything is written.
conflicts.bearing: SR-052 ('nothing is created or changed on the volume'); SR-085.
conflicts.recommendation: Take A. O's order lets the claim file, staging and the log exist before a refusal; the revalidation under the claim closes the race.

conflicts.topic: Missing or unreadable run-state record with a populated backup (Opus call 1)
conflicts.astra: Recover the prior completion date from durable evidence, or refuse.
conflicts.opus: Always rebuild: completion time from the evidence's Written time, a full re-read due, the rebuild reported.
conflicts.bearing: SR-035 (names the change-detection state only), SR-005, SR-082; ruling 'missing change-detection state: re-derive from the backup's record, then report it'.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O: the evidence time is the completion time and the ruling's spirit is 'rebuild and report'. Ask the Owner to confirm that the ruling extends to the run-state record (today the run is refused, value 1).

conflicts.topic: How a stale or foreign change-detection record is caught
conflicts.astra: Bind the record to a source/store identity and a completed generation (new fields).
conflicts.opus: Reconcile per path against the backup's latest record; the backup's values win where they differ.
conflicts.bearing: SR-035; SR-084 (form changes).
conflicts.recommendation: Take O: no new form, and any disagreement with the backup's own record is caught whatever its cause.

conflicts.topic: One path separator and the migration (Opus call 2)
conflicts.astra: Backslash in the record (form); no gap listed.
conflicts.opus: Backslash; lists the gap and the migration: a Linux-written store sees one full rewrite of its latest record and one extra saved state on the first run after the change.
conflicts.bearing: SR-033, SR-136, SR-114; code: a Linux run writes '/' today (confirmed).
conflicts.recommendation: Take the backslash (both agree). The migration is real for container deployments and must be flagged downstream.
conflicts.level: OWNER (a one-time extra saved state in every Linux-written store)

conflicts.astra: An immutable state-format descriptor per state (STATE-FORMAT.json) bound into publication evidence; current states always carry a header-only folder record; kit revision is never age evidence.
conflicts.opus: The state's own kit revision (for missing completeness evidence) and evidence version 3 with DirRows/LinkRows (for folder and link records).
conflicts.recommendation: Hybrid. O's evidence version 3 is immutable (a refresh never copies evidence) and settles folder and link records with no new file. For a state with no evidence at all, O's kit revision fails once a refresh replaces the kit (A's point, and O's own LLR-131), and A's descriptor exists in no state written so far. So the refresh must keep the state's original kit revision readable, or must refuse to refresh a state that predates evidence. Coordinator to choose; the release that introduced evidence must be read from history.
conflicts.level: design (coordinator); owner-visible if a refreshed old state starts refusing

conflicts.topic: Folder record when a state has none
conflicts.astra: Always present, header-only when empty.
conflicts.opus: Present only with rows (today).
conflicts.recommendation: Take O together with evidence DirRows=0 (K14). It keeps today's form, and old kits need no change.

conflicts.astra: Semicolon.
conflicts.opus: Comma (today; both routes split on ',').
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. A semicolon breaks every kit already in a backup for multi-attribute rows.
conflicts.level: design (coordinator); A's value is an error against the code

conflicts.astra: Columns RelativePath, Kind {directory-symlink, junction}, TargetScope {source-relative, external-absolute}, Target (original absolute target).
conflicts.opus: Columns RelativePath, LinkKind {symlink, junction}, TargetClass {inside-source, own-location}, Target (absolute path as resolved at backup time); file LINKS.csv present only with rows.
conflicts.bearing: SR-150, SR-151, SR-152; ruling: an inside link is re-pointed under the target, an own-location link is rebuilt to its original path.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O: its class names are the ruling's two classes. 'Original path' means where the link led, as resolved. A separate file keeps old kits safe (SR-084), as both say.

conflicts.topic: Bounded wait for an unreachable link target
conflicts.astra: 60 seconds per remote resolution or enumeration request.
conflicts.opus: 'The run's bounded wait', no value.
conflicts.bearing: SR-137 ('within the run's bounded wait').
conflicts.recommendation: Take A's value. The SR requires a bound, and only A declares one.

conflicts.astra: Flush the temporary to stable storage before the rename.
conflicts.opus: No flush; a power loss may lose the newest record, reported later as damage.
conflicts.bearing: SR-082 (AC: power removed during writing; 'never a torn one').
conflicts.recommendation: Take A. O's choice contradicts SR-082's AC.

conflicts.astra: A durable publication intent (old and new record identities, required content keys) written before any change.
conflicts.opus: Write order: record temporary, evidence of the temporary, rename record, rename evidence; the next run publishes a matching evidence temporary.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O's write order as the mechanism (minimal, positively identified, no new artifact). Carry A's other concern as its own LLR: earlier content stays reachable until the replacing state is published (orphan ii, gap M53).

conflicts.astra: Revalidate ownership before every publication, move, delete and record replacement.
conflicts.opus: Five fixed boundaries.
conflicts.bearing: SR-144 ('changes no file the successor wrote or published').
conflicts.recommendation: Between O's fences a resumed run can still move or delete. Fence before every destructive step (move, delete, replace, publish). Object creation through a temporary name that never replaces an existing name needs no fence, which keeps the cost off the million-file path.

conflicts.topic: Readers while a writer holds the backup
conflicts.astra: Readers pin a complete generation; writers defer disposal of pinned supply (new read-session form).
conflicts.opus: Readers take no claim and read only published states, which 'never change in place'.
conflicts.recommendation: O's premise is false (repair renames objects, the collapse blanks references and deletes duplicates, a removal deletes a folder). A's pinning needs reader-visible state that the shell route cannot keep. Middle course: no claim and no reader artifact; a reader that finds a location vanished re-resolves by content key, and one that reads a record whose evidence changed mid-read re-reads it (bounded).

conflicts.astra: Refresh the root's kit from the installed program first, then stage a complete kit per state and activate it as a whole.
conflicts.opus: Copy each kit file through a temporary name and rename, never deleting (an older state may then hold both launcher names).
conflicts.bearing: SR-117, SR-110; code: copies the root's existing kit directly, no temporary (confirmed).
conflicts.recommendation: Union: source is the installed program's kit; per-file temporary plus rename, never deleting (O); the revision marker files are written last, so a mixed kit is detectable rather than silent (A's concern, at lower cost).

conflicts.astra: max(90, min(declared cadence, 600) + 30) seconds (up to 630).
conflicts.opus: Declared cadence + 30, between 90 and 600 seconds.
conflicts.bearing: SR-075; code uses A's formula.
conflicts.recommendation: Take A (matches the code; no requirement asks for a change).

conflicts.astra: Exactly 1, true, TRUE, True, yes, YES, Yes.
conflicts.opus: 1, true or yes in any case.
conflicts.bearing: SR-048; the shipped entry script uses A's exact set.
conflicts.recommendation: Take A.

conflicts.astra: All scratch inside the writable working-state mounts; today's host temporary use is a gap.

conflicts.recommendation: Take O. SR-018 forbids truncation, not an appended refusal line, and the appended line is how the owner learns of the refusal.

conflicts.astra: Retired: read-only state is outside the fidelity contract; needed writability is covered by verification and time stamping.
conflicts.opus: Kept under SR-010.
conflicts.bearing: SR-010, SR-056, SR-066. Implementation-born (orphan i), done today on both routes.
conflicts.recommendation: Keep LLR-077 as a child of LLR-056, reworded as: a stored item's protection never blocks verification or the time stamp, and is not handed to the restored file. Its meaning survives, and without it the verification fails on read-only stores.

conflicts.astra: LLR-008 is a parent carrying eight SRs, with children 010, 029, 050, 056 and 068.
conflicts.opus: Flat: each row carries its own SR.
conflicts.bearing: Pointer rules: a child's SR is derived up its chain; one obligation per row.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. Under A's shape every child inherits eight SRs, which blurs coverage and the blast radius.

conflicts.topic: Where the already-compressed type list lives
conflicts.astra: Enumerated in LLR-004.

conflicts.bearing: SR-081 ('a type declared as already compressed').
conflicts.recommendation: Take A's enumeration in LLR-004: the declaration needs one spine home, and the manual is generated from or checked against it.

conflicts.topic: Which files the media rate is measured for
conflicts.astra: Every file for which the tool gives a duration.
conflicts.opus: Each file whose content is read in the run; the rate travels with the entry.
conflicts.bearing: SR-098, SR-113 (run time follows what changed).
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. Running the probe over every file each run breaks SR-113.

conflicts.topic: A restore tool present but failing its self-test at admission
conflicts.astra: (A states tool availability and version as 2, and a known-good probe to tell archive damage from tool failure.)
conflicts.opus: Host fault, 4.
conflicts.bearing: SR-040; ruling: 4 = busy or a host fault mid-work; 2 = needs a person, precondition not met.
conflicts.recommendation: Return 2 at admission. Nothing is mid-work yet, and a retry will not fix a broken tool. O's 4 contradicts the outcome-vocabulary ruling.

conflicts.topic: Writing a stored object where leftovers may sit
conflicts.astra: Write to a private temporary object, verify the content key, publish without replacing any object still claimed.
conflicts.opus: Clear unreferenced debris at the name first, then write (the archive tool appends to an existing archive).
conflicts.recommendation: Take A's temporary-then-publish (no delete on the hot path); O's hazard (appending to debris) cannot occur when the archive is built at a fresh temporary name.

conflicts.astra: The launcher must arrive launchable; a Windows-written kit carried by zip needs a manual chmod today, which falls short of SR-072.
conflicts.opus: 'Runs the shell route without needing an executable bit on the restorer' (true), silent on the launcher's own bit.
conflicts.bearing: SR-072 (double-click on macOS presents a folder choice).
conflicts.recommendation: A is right about the gap (the launcher file says so itself). The fix may lie outside the code (how a kit reaches a Mac), so the Owner decides whether SR-072's double-click holds for zip-transferred kits.

conflicts.topic: Listing location on the backup's volume
conflicts.astra: Not required.
conflicts.opus: Refused when not on the backup's volume (today's code).
conflicts.bearing: SR-063 does not ask. Implementation-born (orphan i).
conflicts.recommendation: Keep only if the browse view's relative links need it (they cannot cross drives on Windows). State that reason in the LLR, or drop the rule.

conflicts.astra: Leaf names (MANIFEST.csv, DIRECTORIES.csv, LINKS.csv, Temp.lock, RUN.inprogress, FileBackupState.json, STATE-FORMAT.json) in LLRs; interfaces state roles.
conflicts.opus: Names in the interface form; LLRs refer to them by role.
conflicts.bearing: Brief: on-disk data names that are the agreed form are allowed in interface data; single home.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O. The name is form, both sides spell it, and a rename then touches one row.

conflicts.topic: Folder-only or link-only change and the saved state
conflicts.astra: A difference in the folder or link record is a change and keeps a saved state.
conflicts.opus: Change set is files plus heals; silent on folder-only changes.
conflicts.bearing: SR-005 ('when a run changes the backed-up state'), SR-065.
conflicts.recommendation: Take A. The folder record is part of the backed-up state; today a new empty folder alone discards the prior folder record (gap M48).

conflicts.astra: Store coordination and content resolution as top-level components; capture and change detection one component; container adapter under launch.
conflicts.opus: Guard under the backup engine; index under removal; restore search under entry restoration; capture and change detection separate; container on its own.
conflicts.bearing: Responsibilities the SRs demand; the kit-independence rule.
conflicts.recommendation: Take O's tree (proposed tree above). A's shared 'content resolution' would make the restore kit depend on the backup-side index unless it moves into the store format; revisit only if K22 goes A's way.

design_gaps.code: The walk neither follows a folder link nor records one; no link record exists; neither restore route recreates a link. File links are followed.
design_gaps.settled: O's inference is consistent with the code: the walk lists a folder link with no files beneath it, so it is probably written to the folder record as an empty folder.

design_gaps.code: A backup or saved-state location overlapping a source is not refused. The listing location is checked only when the view is on, per location during the run, failing it (1). State-location overlap is checked only against its own set, failing it (1). Roots are created before these checks.
No up-front writability check; the run works, then fails when the change-detection record is written (1).
A missing record is silently treated as empty; a malformed one throws and fails the location; its evidence is never checked on read; a stale or foreign record is trusted wherever size and time match.
design_gaps.settled: Settled for O: missing means empty (no refusal). A's 'refuses malformed state' concerns the run-state record (M05).

design_gaps.code: A populated backup whose run-state record is missing or unparseable is refused (location fails, 1).
A saved state is named by the previous run's start time; LastBackupRun stores a time taken near the run's start.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code; A missed it.

design_gaps.code: Calendar-boundary decision; N with no recorded re-read does re-read; the re-read time is stamped whenever a re-read was due, including runs with unreadable folders.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code; O's design followed the code (conflict K01).

design_gaps.code: A backup returns 1 for busy, capacity, retired form and empty source, and 3 only for witness mismatch; the saved-state report always returns 0; unhandled errors in removal or the report get no mapped value; non-backup actions and both restorers' classified exits are gated by -ExitCode.
design_gaps.settled: Settled: the backup's own exit is not gated by -ExitCode (A over-generalised); configuration failures, non-backup actions and the restorers are.

design_gaps.code: Every claim failure is one refusal (backup 1, removal 2); contention and I/O are not told from denial or an unusable location; the holder is not reliably named.
Every leftover refusal fails the location with 1; an unfinished removal's refusal does not name re-running it as the remedy.
design_gaps.settled: A's G-14 touches only the lock side.

design_gaps.code: The empty-source refusal fails the location with 1, not 2.
The demand is per location set, content only (no records, kits, logs, temporary space or allocation), checked after roots, claim, log and staging exist; a shortfall fails the location with 1.
A backup over a retired form fails with 1; the shell route checks the retired form after creating the target and its log; an unrecognised marker or header is not refused as a form.
No backup-side runtime-version check.

Obtaining the hashing component prompts when attended and needs -AutoInstallDeps when unattended; the fetched package is not checked against a digest; a missing optional tool may prompt; redirected or closed input is not detected.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code (no digest check found).

design_gaps.code: If the kit's hashing library is missing, the language-runtime restore falls back to a package-source install with a prompt, even with -NonInteractive.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed.

design_gaps.code: The language-runtime route checks neither its runtime version nor the kit's hashing library before writing; the shell route checks the archive extractor only after creating the target.
design_gaps.settled: Second clause from the code check.

design_gaps.code: The language-runtime route normalises the path lexically first (a parent component is cancelled, not refused), resolves only the deepest existing component, and falls back to the text when resolution fails; on GNU systems the shell route accepts a parent component through its resolver.
design_gaps.settled: Both sides right; each saw part.

design_gaps.code: Both routes leave compressed entries out of the demand and add no allowance; the language-runtime route creates the target and its log before the space and archive-tool checks; an unmeasurable volume is skipped (silently on that route).
Absent evidence is excused for every state; no positive age evidence is consulted; the shell route silently skips non-numeric Rows or Bytes.
An escaping entry is counted as missing content (1), not a damaged record (3); an escaping folder-record row only warns.

Collisions are not detected: on Windows the language-runtime route keeps the last of two case-differing rows; elsewhere both are written to one file; the shell route lets the second overwrite the first.

A missing or malformed folder record never changes the outcome; nothing tells a state that should have one from one that has none; the language-runtime route assigns attributes (replacing existing bits); the shell route never applies attributes, only logs them.
design_gaps.settled: Shell-route clause from the code check; neither side listed it.

design_gaps.code: A blank time is skipped silently and an unparseable one only warns; the restore still ends complete.

An unclassified error mid-restore reports 2 although files were written; a shell switch without its value exits 127; a direct object's expansion failure is a host failure (4) with no tool self-test (the self-test runs only in the pool search); a missing item whose search ends in a host cause is recorded as missing content.
design_gaps.settled: A found the direct-expansion case, O the rest.

design_gaps.code: The summaries give counts and names but no per-entry causes (causes only in separate log lines); the report entries are not in the IF-022 form.
The record gives one new-or-changed count and a removed count; added files are not told from changed ones and most are not named.
No progress entries at all; the only periodic activity is the owner-record refresh.
A file that cannot be read for its digest aborts the whole location; retries cover only the copy.
The default check reads only an object's opening bytes; altered content is found only with -Deep.
Repair renames and rewrites forms but never copies content back from a verified copy elsewhere.
The refresh copies the backup root's existing kit into each saved state (it does not regenerate it from the installed program), file by file with no temporary name, so a kill can leave a mixed kit.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code; O had left it unconfirmed. Whether each repair rename publishes by temporary and rename is still unconfirmed.

design_gaps.code: No space view and no setting for it.
The media rate is never computed: the switch that would enable the tool is hard-wired off, and no record entry says the measure was not taken.
design_gaps.settled: Settled for O: the measurement function is called per hashed file but returns nothing because the tool is never resolved. A's 'invokes measurement when the tool is available' is wrong.

design_gaps.code: No licence or notice file in any backup; the hashing library is redistributed without its notice.
The container image carries no notices file.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed from the image build definition (A had not read it).

design_gaps.code: The native-Windows form carries no version and the helper writes none.
The native-Windows form gets a shape check only: no closed key set, no strict value kinds; the published description covers JSON only.
A native-Windows credential in plain text is not refused.
A multi-set JSON configuration draws a warning; removal, report, check and view act on the first set only.
design_gaps.settled: First-set clause from O, confirmed.

design_gaps.code: Removal and the report resolve locations in the backup's mode: they need the source to exist and create missing backup or saved-state folders.
A Linux run writes '/' where a Windows run writes '\'; a run from the other host type then sees every file removed and added.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed; A's record form says backslash but A listed no gap. Migration: K13.

design_gaps.code: The evidence is written only after the record is renamed, and nothing is flushed; a kill between the two leaves a mismatch the next run refuses.
design_gaps.settled: Flush clause from A.

design_gaps.code: The quick start's first run asks before installing the hashing component; the helper writes an unversioned document; the user manual states two different current configuration versions.
The time and memory budgets have never been measured at the declared scale; removal and the audit keep whole records; restore recovery scans candidates per unresolved row.
design_gaps.settled: Not a measured failure: a missing measurement.

design_gaps.code: The repair's findings document has no per-finding Repaired field (a fresh re-check is printed instead).

With the change-detection record at the source root, the whole backup infrastructure list is excluded at the source root (owner files sharing a backup-only name are skipped); with the record elsewhere, that branch also skips the volume-root filter.
design_gaps.settled: A's claim, not re-checked by the alignment; confirm when the code is headed.

design_gaps.code: The saved-state decision comes from the file-row diff only; a run whose only change is a new empty folder adds no saved state and overwrites the folder record.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code.

design_gaps.code: A removal killed before its commit point leaves its staging marker; the next removal refuses any existing staging area and backups refuse the marker, so the store wedges until a person clears it.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code.

design_gaps.code: Target checks are lexical (a link to outside is not resolved); module-level options can waive the unreferenced-content and evidence refusals.

Removed and superseded objects move into staging before the new latest record is published; a kill there leaves a witnessed latest record whose bytes only staging holds, and no restore searches staging.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed in code; O missed it.

design_gaps.code: A file of exactly 262144 bytes is measured; the SR gives files at or below 256 KiB the file-type rule.
design_gaps.settled: Confirmed (both code conditions treat 262144 as above the floor).

design_gaps.code: A Windows-written kit carried to a Mac by zip needs a manual chmod before Finder opens the launcher; the restorer holds the window on success and on classified exits but not on its error trap.
design_gaps.settled: Hold-on-trap clause from the code check. See K34.

design_gaps.code: The language-runtime route never checks for a desktop session (only the console and input), and a cancelled folder choice falls back to a typed prompt.
design_gaps.settled: Found by the alignment's code check.

design_gaps.code: The owner identity is re-checked at five boundaries only; a resumed former owner can still move or delete between them.
design_gaps.settled: A gap under the recommended K21 design.

design_gaps.code: A reader meeting a location that a concurrent repair, collapse or removal has just moved has no re-resolution or re-read rule.
design_gaps.settled: Reworded to the recommended K22 design.

design_gaps.code: Scratch uses the host temporary folder; the shipped compose file mounts /tmp as tmpfs.
design_gaps.settled: Remains a gap only if SR-130's wording excludes a non-persistent scratch mount (K26).
